newsitem.title: GERMANY: German pig, potato futures promising - farm chief.
newsitem.headline: German pig, potato futures promising - farm chief.

text.p: Germany's new pig and potato futures contracts are set for success when they start up in the fourth quarter of 1997, former president of German farm union DBV Constantin Freiherr Heereman said on Monday.

There was also scope for another European rapeseed contract to complement the one on the French Matif exchange, he said in remarks prepared for delivery at the Hanover stock exchange, which will house the futures bourse.

The success of a planned wheat futures contract may be limited by the extent of continued management of the market by Brussels legislators, he said. However, this was not unwelcome in order to protect farmers interests.
"I trust management at WTB (the holding company of the new exchange) will introduce the right futures contract at the right time," Heereman said.
"It is also important that the banks get more involved and that we get a precise start-up date as soon as possible."
Heereman said EU pork markets offered ideal conditions for futures -- dramatic and unexpected supply and demand factors as well as price volatility.

Prices soared in 1997 amid Dutch supply reductions in a severe outbreak of swine fever, much to the benefit of German pig farmers who usually compete with the Dutch. Dutch slaughterings may be down by a third for the next 12 months while Danish exports were redirected from Germany to Japan, where there is a shortfall.

German producers earned up to 4.40 marks per kg at the end of April/early May, 60 percent more than at the start of 1997. But many had started to expand the pig population and this should sooner or later weigh on prices.
The meat industry was now keen to lock in lower prices.

In potatoes, Germany led the EU with 10-13 million tonnes annually out of a total 45-50 million tonnes. Heereman said the Matif potato contract had failed because of stable prices and because it was based on an unimportant variety.
WTB experts had drawn up a contract based on a basket of leading types with similar prices, but guided by the cheapest. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
